messages:
elaine: quick thread 1) do we standardize on a single canonical billing id for all telemetry (charge_id) derived at ingress, or 2) allow services to emit their own billing tags and resolve later? thinking about multi-model routing + cross-account joins.

kai: canonical at ingress seems safer for rollback + cross-region joins. if apps emit different tags we end up with mismatch and weird double-billing risk.

priya: agree but must be deterministic. propose derivation rules: tenant_id + api_key_hash + model_family -> charge_id. store derivation_version on envelope.

matt: question: what about per-request overrides? e.g., invoice overrides from enterprise customers. need a safe override path that is auditable.

elaine: design: router computes canonical charge_id by default. if service includes override header X-Billing-Override, router will sign and attach override_proof (HMAC) so downstream can trust it. rollback: if proof invalid, drop override and emit alert.

priya: for validation we should gate overrides via a whitelisted tenant flag. only tenants with enterprise-entitlement can set overrides. prevents accidental misuse.

kai: storage implications: we should keep minimal keys in hot-path: charge_id, tenant_id, ingest_version, envelope_ts, token_count. everything else goes to async enrich topic. this keeps write tail latency low.

matt: enrichment window: how long do we wait for enrichment before considering fields permanently missing? 1h? 24h? shorter windows reduce complexity for billing but increase missing debug info.

elaine: leaning toward 12h default with pluggable policy per-tenant. high-value tenants can request longer windows; default SRE policy 12h to cap repair/backfill.

priya: implies query semantics: billing queries MUST operate on charge_id only. If enrichment arrives later and adds model_tag or app_label, queries that need those can either join to enrichment table (best-effort) or use backfilled tags. note audit queries need to surface 'was_enriched' flag.

kai: implementation sketch (router pseudocode):
```
charge_id = derive_charge(tenant, api_key, model_hash, derivation_v1)
if X-Billing-Override present and tenant.whitelisted:
  if verify_hmac(override_proof): charge_id = override_payload.charge_id
  else emit_alert('bad-override-proof', envelope_id)
write_hotpath({charge_id, tenant_id, ingest_version, ts, tokens})
publish_async(full_payload, topic='telemetry-enrich')
```

matt: ops: add metric `enrichment_lag_p50/p95/p99`, and `override_reject_rate`. set pager at enrichment_lag_p99 > 2h for more than 15m.

elaine: migration story: we will tag old envelopes with ingest_version=v0. new routers write v1. Query layer will coerce v0 envelopes into canonical_space using best-effort heuristics during a 30d migration window. After 30d we'll run permanent reconciliation for any discrepancies.

priya: also add a lightweight forensic job that for top 100k envelopes/day cross-checks resolved charge_id between router and enrichment to catch derivation bugs.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for tag=chargeid-ingest-v1 in cluster=us-central at 4356900100 by kai

kai: i'll open the PR today with derivation code + CI tests. priyas: can you add the query examples for backfilled joins?

priya: yup will add sample SQL and a note about performance tradeoffs.

matt: i'll draft SRE runbook and alerts. also proposing a circuit-breaker: if async topic backlog > 1M messages, router temporarily switches to enriched-rich-ingest mode for safety window.

elaine: last: we need to document legal/finance consequences of override usage. i'll loop in legal/product after schema PR. thanks everyone :rocket:

kai: ping in thread when PR up.

priya: thanks, signing off.
